raw_case_text: A 57-year-old male patient presented for 2 years multiple nodules and tumors of cystic consistence on the back of right foot and right leg (Figure 1). The lesions exhibited a sporotrichosis-like distribution pattern but there was no history of local trauma. The patient received a kidney transplant 4 years ago due to hypertensive nephropathy and his immunosuppressive treatment included azathioprine, tacrolimus and prednisone. The initial diagnostic hypotheses were sporotrichosis, paracoccidioidomycosis, leishmaniasis and phaeohyphomycosis. Direct mycological examination revealed irregular and septate moniliform hyphae of pigmented fungi. Culture on Sabouraud-Agar with chloramphenicol demonstrated vegetative chambered hyphae with septate annellophores, compatible with Exophiala sp. At the histopathological test a granulomatous inflammatory infiltrate was observed, in the form of brownish walls composed of giant multinucleated cells with fungal structures (Figure 2). Specific staining demonstrated pheomelanin in the fungi walls (Fontana-Masson) and search for fungi was positive (Gridley) (Figure 3). The patient was treated first with voriconazole 200mg 12/12h associated with surgical excision of lesions. During treatment with voriconazole the patient developed a severe clinical picture of hyponatremia; the drug was replaced with itraconazole 200mg/day, which was used during five months, with no relapses since then.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 57-year-old male renal transplant recipient presented with a 2-year history of multiple cystic nodules and tumoral lesions arranged in a sporotrichoid distribution along his right foot and right leg.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the preceding 2 years, the patient developed multiple cystic nodules and tumors on the dorsum of his right foot ascending along the right leg without recalled local trauma.
subjective.past_medical_history: Hypertensive nephropathy status post renal transplantation 4 years prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Home immunosuppressive regimen included azathioprine, tacrolimus, and prednisone.

objective.physical_examination: Multiple nodules and tumors of cystic consistency distributed in a lymphocutaneous (sporotrichosis-like) pattern over the dorsum of the right foot and right lower extremity.
objective.routine_investigations: Direct mycological examination revealed irregular, septate, pigmented moniliform hyphae; Sabouraud-chloramphenicol agar culture grew chambered vegetative hyphae with septate annellophores characteristic of Exophiala sp.
objective.advanced_workup: Skin biopsy histopathology (H&E, Fontana-Masson, and Gridley stains) demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with brownish cyst walls, multinucleated giant cells, and melanin-containing fungal elements.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Differential diagnoses of sporotrichosis, paracoccidioidomycosis, and cutaneous leishmaniasis were excluded by direct microscopy, Fontana-Masson/Gridley histopathology, and mycological culture confirming subcutaneous phaeohyphomycosis caused by Exophiala sp. Combined surgical excision and oral voriconazole (200 mg twice daily, switched to oral itraconazole 200 mg/day for 5 months due to voriconazole-induced severe hyponatremia) achieved complete cure without relapse.
